name: playwright
description: Token-cheap browser automation over @playwright/cli (hp): isolated in-memory profile by default, files only under an output dir, and CDP attach to a running Chrome behind a /dev/tty typed-echo gate with --attached-writes on every page action there
hits: any web page (an open-world browser); optionally a running Chrome over CDP
surface: CLI `hp` + `lib/playwright.js`. Reads (snapshot/screenshot/pdf/console/network/storage reads) are free. Page actions and navigations (open/goto/reload/go-back/go-forward included) run free on the isolated profile and need the loud bare `--attached-writes` on any attached session; `open` on an attached session is refused. `connect` to a real profile (`--cdp=chrome`, a foreign endpoint, `--extension`) makes the human type the target back at /dev/tty, or stages for `toolbelt approve playwright <code>`; an endpoint `launch-debug` opened (tool-owned profile) attaches ungated, but page actions on it need --attached-writes like any attached session. No verb prints a cookie or token value; `kill-all`, `delete-data`, `cookie-get`'s value-printing siblings beyond the listed set are not exposed

origin.note: hello-playwright workshop (thin execSync wrapper + examples + docs). The belt replaced the wrapper's shell-string exec with an argv spawn through hp.mjs, pinned @playwright/cli locally instead of a global install, moved the config to .playwright/cli.config.json with isolated: true, and added connect/launch-debug/approve/status with the gates described in safeguards[]

install.description: Install @playwright/cli (and playwright-core) locally from the committed lockfile
install.why: hp shells out to node_modules/.bin/playwright-cli; the attach/detach verbs need >= 0.1.18, which a global install may not be
install.yes: node_modules/ is created inside tools/playwright from package-lock.json; no browser is downloaded (hp uses the installed Google Chrome channel)
install.no: skipped; every hp verb except --help, status and the unit tests fails with the npm install hint

env.name: HP_HOME
env.description: hp's record dir (default ~/.cache/hello-playwright, mode 700): sessions.json (endpoint labels for status and audit lines), audit.log, pending/ staged connects, launched/ Chrome records, profiles/ launch-debug user-data dirs. Not a gate input: whether a session is attached is read from playwright-cli's own registry (keyed to tools/playwright, under the OS cache dir), and nothing under HP_HOME can narrow the gate — every attached session needs --attached-writes

env.name: PLAYWRIGHT_OUTPUT_DIR
env.description: The only directory screenshots, PDFs, snapshots and saved storage state may land in (default tools/playwright/output, gitignored)

env.name: CHROME_PATH
env.description: Chrome binary for launch-debug; default search: Chrome for Testing, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge

env.name: PLAYWRIGHT_CLI_SESSION
env.description: Default session name for lib/playwright.js callers; hp itself always passes -s explicitly and strips this from the child environment

auth.flow: No credential of its own. The isolated profile starts empty every time; anything you sign into there lives in memory until close. An attached browser (connect) carries every session the operator is logged into in that Chrome — all of them at once, under the operator's own identity — which is why attaching is the gated verb

caches.note: launch-debug user-data dirs (700). Whatever you sign into in a launched Chrome persists here; a cookie-encryption key separate from your real profile's. Never your real Chrome profile
port → pid/profile records for Chromes hp spawned; no secret, but marks which loopback endpoints are the tool's own

safeguards: Isolated by default, and only that config: .playwright/cli.config.json sets browser.isolated=true with no cdpEndpoint/userDataDir, runCli() in hp.mjs pins `--config` to that file on open/attach and strips every PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_*/PLAYWRIGHT_CLI_* variable from the child environment, and findRefusedFlag() exits 2 before anything runs when any verb carries --config, --persistent, --profile, --user-data-dir, --storage-state, --cdp, --endpoint, --extension or --session (connect keeps --cdp/--endpoint/--extension; launch-debug keeps --profile as a name). findRefusedFlag() also refuses every single-character flag key (`--s`, `--g`, `--h`, `--v` are upstream aliases; `--s=real` is `--session=real`) and any positional that starts with a dash, including everything after `--` and negative numbers, because hp forwards positionals verbatim and upstream's parser reads `-s=real`, `--config=x` or `-1` there as options. So no read verb can reach a persistent profile or a CDP endpoint, no page action can be re-pointed at an attached session, and the real Chrome user-data-dir is never a valid profile anywhere (validProfileName accepts one path segment under $HP_HOME/profiles/)

connect to a real profile (cmdConnect in hp.mjs: --cdp=chrome|msedge, any endpoint hp did not launch, --extension) prints what attaching exposes, then requires the target typed back on /dev/tty — never stdin; --yes/--force are usage errors; with no terminal it stages the request to $HP_HOME/pending/<code>.json (dir 700, file 600, O_EXCL, 15-minute expiry) and exits 3 with `toolbelt approve playwright <code>`

approve (cmdApprove) opens /dev/tty, shows the staged target, takes the typed echo, replays the connect in-process through a one-shot module-level approval no env var or flag can set, and deletes the record whether or not the attach succeeded; no terminal → exit 4, record kept, never auto-approved

An endpoint hp itself launched (launch-debug record under $HP_HOME/launched/ with a live pid) attaches without the typed-echo gate because no session of yours is in that profile; once attached it is gated like every attached session (page actions need --attached-writes), since upstream records no endpoint and hp's records are caller-writable, so hp cannot prove which browser an attached session is on

Page actions and navigations on an attached session (VERBS.interact in hp.mjs: open/goto/reload/go-back/go-forward, click/fill/eval/…) exit 2 without the bare --attached-writes (a value form such as --attached-writes=false is exit 2); the flag is loud and always honored (SENSIBILITIES #2 — a deliberate act is never refused) and every such call writes an audit line; snapshot/screenshot/console/network stay free. Attached-ness is asked of playwright-cli itself (cliAttached(): `list --json`, the registry the action runs against, keyed to the tool dir and outside $HP_HOME) immediately before every page action; if that call fails or returns no browsers[] the action exits 2. Any session playwright-cli reports attached needs the flag — launch-debug Chromes included — because upstream records no endpoint and $HP_HOME is writable by the caller, so no hp record narrows the gate (sessions.json supplies only the endpoint label). runCli() strips PWTEST_* (which relocates that registry) along with PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_*/PLAYWRIGHT_CLI_*. The unit tests reach a fresh record dir only through main()'s in-process env override, which no CLI flag or variable maps to
Every --filename (screenshot, pdf, snapshot, state-save) is resolved by containFilename() under PLAYWRIGHT_OUTPUT_DIR; an absolute path or a `..` segment is exit 2 and nothing runs
classifyEndpoint() refuses a non-loopback CDP endpoint without --remote-ok; channels and loopback URLs only by default

launch-debug spawns Chrome only with --user-data-dir under $HP_HOME/profiles/<name> and --remote-debugging-port, waits for /json/version, kills the process on timeout, and records pid+port; `hp close` detaches an attached session (the external browser keeps running) and quits only a Chrome hp launched

Audit line (audit() in hp.mjs) to stderr and $HP_HOME/audit.log (600) on connect, detach, launch-debug, close-of-launched and every --attached-writes action: timestamp, verb, session, endpoint, profile class, result — never page content or cookie values (SENSIBILITIES #7)
The verb table is an allowlist: kill-all, delete-data, show, devtools, tracing/video and the skill installer are not reachable through hp; an unknown verb exits 2 and runs nothing
playwright-cli is invoked with an argv array (spawnSync), never a shell string, and with NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1 so the wrapper makes no registry call of its own
Ceilings are code constants (EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS 60s per call, LAUNCH_WAIT_MS 15s, PENDING_TTL_S 15 min); the test suite asserts them (SENSIBILITIES #3)

verbs.name: open
verbs.note: isolated in-memory profile, config pinned to .playwright/cli.config.json; --headed to watch; --config/--persistent/--profile are exit 2. On a session playwright-cli reports attached it is exit 2 even with --attached-writes, because upstream would stop (detach) that session to start a fresh browser; `close` is the verb for detaching

verbs.name: goto
verbs.note: a navigation under the operator's cookies (logout, unsubscribe, OAuth consent, admin URLs) is an authenticated action: free on the isolated profile, --attached-writes + audit line on an attached session

verbs.name: go-back
verbs.note: as goto

verbs.name: go-forward
verbs.note: as goto

verbs.name: reload
verbs.note: as goto

verbs.name: snapshot
verbs.note: accessibility tree with refs; --filename lands under the output dir

verbs.name: screenshot
verbs.note: --filename lands under the output dir only

verbs.name: pdf
verbs.note: --filename lands under the output dir only

verbs.name: cookie-list
verbs.note: names/domains of the session's cookies; on an attached real profile this lists your real cookies — treat the output as a secret

verbs.name: cookie-get
verbs.note: one cookie's value; same caution as cookie-list

verbs.name: state-save
verbs.note: writes cookies+storage to a file under the output dir only; that file is a session credential — do not commit or share it

verbs.name: status
verbs.note: what playwright-cli reports as attached (the gate's input), hp's endpoint records, and which Chromes hp launched; no network

verbs.name: launch-debug
verbs.note: Chrome on a loopback debugging port with --user-data-dir under $HP_HOME/profiles/<name>; never the default user-data-dir; prints the endpoint. connect to it is ungated; page actions on it still need --attached-writes

verbs.name: close
verbs.note: detaches a session playwright-cli reports attached (external browser keeps running); quits a Chrome hp launched; else closes the isolated browser

verbs.name: click
verbs.note: free on the isolated (non-attached) profile; --attached-writes required on any session playwright-cli reports attached, launch-debug Chromes included

verbs.name: upload
verbs.note: sends a local file to the page: egress even on the isolated profile

verbs.name: eval
verbs.note: arbitrary JS in the page

verbs.name: run-code
verbs.note: arbitrary Playwright code against the session

verbs.name: tab-close
verbs.note: on an attached browser this closes one of the operator's real tabs

verbs.name: cookie-clear
verbs.note: on an attached real profile this signs you out everywhere in that browser

verbs.name: connect
verbs.note: -s <name> --cdp=<chrome|msedge|url> | --extension | --endpoint=<ws>; real profile: type the target back at /dev/tty, no --yes, headless → staged for `toolbelt approve playwright <code>`; an endpoint launch-debug opened attaches ungated (its page actions are still gated); non-loopback refused without --remote-ok

verbs.name: approve
verbs.note: what `toolbelt approve playwright <code>` runs: shows the staged target, takes the typed echo on /dev/tty, attaches once, deletes the record; no terminal → exit 4

verbs.name: attach to the real Chrome profile by launching it with a debugging port
verbs.note: launch-debug accepts only a profile name under $HP_HOME/profiles/; Chrome >= 136 ignores --remote-debugging-port on the default user-data-dir anyway. The only real-profile routes are the human flipping chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging or installing the Bridge extension, then `hp connect` through the typed-echo gate

verbs.name: kill-all / delete-data / show / devtools / tracing / video
verbs.note: exist in playwright-cli; hp's verb allowlist does not forward them

risk.worst_case: after a human typed the target at /dev/tty and passed --attached-writes per action, an agent clicks or evaluates JS in the operator's real, fully signed-in Chrome under the operator's name — any site, no per-site gate; on the isolated default profile the worst case is a form submitted on the open web from an empty, anonymous browser

systems.name: Web browser (Playwright, isolated profile)
systems.read: node hp.mjs open https://example.com && node hp.mjs snapshot

checks.fix: cd {TOOLBELT}/tools/playwright && npm install   (or: toolbelt setup playwright) — installs @playwright/cli 0.1.18+ locally; the attach/detach verbs need it

checks.label: state dir ~/.cache/hello-playwright writable (created on first use)

smoke_test.command: node hp.mjs --help >/dev/null && node hp.mjs status >/dev/null && node hp.mjs -s=toolbelt-smoke connect --cdp=chrome --explain >/dev/null && node --test test/hp.test.mjs
smoke_test.expect: help and status render; the connect --explain pre-flight prints the gate text and attaches nothing; unit tests green — tiering vs manifest, filename containment, loopback rule, staging, typed echo, --attached-writes read from playwright-cli's registry (a fresh HP_HOME, forged sessions.json+launched/ records, a launch-debug attach and a failed `list` all still refuse), navigation verbs gated, open refused on an attached session, single-character flag keys (`--s=real`) and option-like positionals after `--` refused, `--attached-writes=<value>` refused, approve replay, launch-debug profile refusal, refused re-pointing flags (--config/--persistent/--profile/--cdp/--session), config pin and PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_*/PWTEST_* env strip. The tests isolate hp's records through main()'s in-process env override, never an env var. No browser, no network
